summary: TypeScript SDK: tool-call idempotency header dropped when relayed to customer webhook, causing duplicate tool executions
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when using the TypeScript SDK in streaming mode with function/tool calling enabled, the idempotency metadata (idempotency key/nonce) that the SDK sets on outgoing tool call requests is not being forwarded by our webhook relay to the customer's webhook endpoint. Impact:
- Customers observe duplicate side-effects: third-party webhooks called twice for the same logical tool invocation (e.g., duplicate order creations).
- Appears surface-level: tool call completes, external webhook receives 2 POSTs within <500ms.
Environment:
- StencilAI (dedicated account) on prod-us-east
- SDK: @redwood/sdk-js v2.7.4 (ts build)
- Relay: internal webhook-relay v1.9.0 behind api-gateway
- Model: redwood/gpt-6b, streaming via ws+chunked function_call JSON frames
Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Create a tool that posts to a webhook and requires an idempotency token header (X-Idempotency-Key) to dedupe POSTs.
2) In TS client, start a streaming generate with function_call enabled and include an explicit idempotency value in the tool_call options (sdk sets tool_call.metadata.idempotency_key).
3) Simulate a transient network interruption - disconnect the client briefly and allow the SDK to reconnect and re-send a resume request.
4) Observe webhook endpoint logs: two POSTs for the same tool execution ID but only the second POST contains the idempotency header (first POST lacking the header).
Observed behavior:
- Relay forwards the function_call body and invokes the webhook twice. The first invocation is missing the idempotency header, so the customer's webhook cannot dedupe and executes twice.
Expected behavior:
- Relay should preserve and forward idempotency metadata (either as header X-Idempotency-Key or a predictable webhook payload field) for every invocation of a tool call, including resumptions and replayed stream frames.
Temporary workaround:
- Customer added server-side dedupe by correlating tool_call.payload.order_reference with a store lookup. This mitigates duplicates but requires app changes.
- Recommended short-term: ask customer to enable "require-idempotency-header" on their webhook and reject calls without header (not ideal for them).
Notes: customer provided webhook logs and sample wire captures attached in comments.

Check webhook logs for duplicate POSTs and missing idempotency header on first call

2026-03-10 10:05 - Diego Marquez (engineering): Initial triage - reproduced locally with sdk-js v2.7.4 + relay v1.9.0. Observe that resume frames go through a different relay path that currently reconstructs tool_call payload but does not copy transient metadata headers by default.
2026-03-10 15:44 - Customer (StencilAI): We can reproduce in staging and prod. This is causing duplicate orders; urgent. Agreed to apply temporary dedupe on our side while you investigate.

2026-03-11 11:20 - Diego Marquez: Added hypothesis: relay path for 'stream-resume' used proto-level replay handler that reconstructs HTTP request from body and only includes canonical headers. Missing code path to attach tool_call.metadata.* into X-* headers. Creating patch to copy metadata.idempotency_key into X-Idempotency-Key for all relay invocations.

2026-03-12 08:03 - Diego Marquez: Patch submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/relay/pull/88. Running integration tests against streaming resume scenarios. Coordinating with SDK team to add an opt-in header name mapping until patch is released.
2026-03-12 12:15 - Customer: Acknowledged. Will keep temporary dedupe active and wait for fix. Please advise ETA for patch rollout.
investigation_notes: Reproduced with local harness using ws-based streaming + resume causing the relay to use the replay code path
Observed that initial 'live' tool_call includes headers map derived from request.extensions, but resume uses a reconstructed payload without the extensions map
Unit tests missed this scenario because they use non-resume flow
Hypothesis: relay v1.9.0 lost transient metadata when converting from internal tool_call envelope to outbound HTTP request during resume
resolution_notes: Patch prepared in relay to preserve/propagate tool_call.metadata.idempotency_key as X-Idempotency-Key for all outbound webhook invocations, including replay/resume flows. PR #88 created; integration tests added to cover resume + metadata propagation. Plan: deploy relay v1.9.1 to staging 2026-03-13 and to prod 2026-03-14 after 48h observation. Also working with SDK team to add explicit header mapping utility in @redwood/sdk-js v2.7.5 so customers can configure header name used for idempotency keys.
follow_up_actions: Merge relay PR #88 and run canary in us-east
Publish @redwood/sdk-js v2.7.5 with header mapping helper and docs update
Confluence: add runbook entry for webhook idempotency header loss during stream resume
Reach out to StencilAI post-deploy to validate and confirm duplicate behavior resolved
resolution_status: Fix in progress - awaiting canary results
customer_impact_summary: Duplicate external webhook calls leading to duplicated business side-effects (orders); customer deployed application-level dedupe as workaround; P1 because duplicates occur in production and affect revenue-critical flows
